chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Being upright for God, not associating partners with Him' [22:31]. He said: 'The upright way (hanifiyya) is from the natural disposition (fitra) upon which God created the people; there is no alteration in God's creation' [30:30]. He said: 'He created them with the recognition (ma'rifa) of Him.'

Zurara said: And I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their offspring, and made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes!' — the verse [7:172]. He said: 'He extracted from the back of Adam his offspring until the Day of Resurrection. They came out like particles, and He introduced Himself to them and showed them Himself. Had it not been for that, not one of them would have recognized his Lord.'

And he said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Every newborn is born upon the fitra — meaning the recognition that God, Mighty and Majestic, is his Creator. Likewise is His saying: "And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say: God"' [31:25].

key_terms.الحنيفية: Hanifiyya — the pure monotheistic way of Abraham, identified as part of fitra
key_terms.الفطرة: Fitra — the innate natural disposition with which every human is created; specifically identified here as the recognition (ma'rifa) of God as Creator
key_terms.المعرفة: Ma'rifa — direct recognition/gnosis of God, distinguished from mere intellectual belief
key_terms.ميثاق الألست: The Covenant of Alast (7:172) — the pre-eternal covenant when all souls testified to God's lordship

ai.seo_question: What is fitra in Islam and how does it relate to the recognition of God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) interprets three Quranic verses (22:31, 7:172, 31:25) to establish that the innate human disposition (fitra) is fundamentally the recognition of God as Creator. In this teaching, delivered to his trusted companion Zurara, the Imam explains that the Covenant of Alast (7:172) was a primordial event where all human souls — taken from Adam's loins — witnessed God directly, making monotheistic recognition a permanent feature of human nature. This explains the Prophet's famous hadith that every child is born upon the fitra.
